name: Spiral fitter, global winding fit
superseded_note: Kept because a frozen profile stays readable: this is what the integration could do before the scroll was selectable. 0.2.0 rebinds the six module constants and runs from the P1 queue; nothing should be queued against this one.

source.note: The volume_cartographer source-lock commit the villa image already pins, so this backend adds no second source identity to keep true.

not_selectable_here.dataset_path: Module-level constant '/ephemeral/paul/spiral/dataset' at the pinned commit. No FIT_SPIRAL_* variable reaches it; a different dataset means presenting it at that path or editing the script.
not_selectable_here.z_begin: Module-level constant 4000. The tutorial describes setting a z range, but z_begin is not a default_config key, so it is not an override.
not_selectable_here.z_end: Module-level constant 17000, same reason as z_begin.
not_selectable_here.spiral_outward_sense: Module-level constant 'CW'; the winding direction is a property of the scroll and is not parameterised.

outputs.note: The per-winding TIFXYZ is what makes this a P1 backend at all: it is the same artifact seed-grow produces, so it enters the same P2 certification gate rather than a parallel one.

notes.config_overrides: disable_patches only, which is the basic workflow the tutorial describes -- fit on point collections and tracks, load no verified or unverified patches. Every other one of the 105 keys is left at upstream's default, frozen for comparability rather than tuned.
notes.gpu: Required. This is a fitting run, not a local grow.
notes.status: EXPERIMENTAL_NOT_DEFAULT because no frozen reference control has compared this backend against vc3d-m7-seed-grow on this corpus, and because at this commit the scroll cannot be selected through the profile.

non_claims: a fitted spiral is not physical-QC acceptance, not ink, and not text; it is geometry and enters the same certification gate as any other surface
no comparison against vc3d-m7-seed-grow has been run on this corpus; this profile exists so that comparison can be made and records nothing about which backend is better
the required_inputs above are the paths the script reads at the pinned commit, not a claim that Campaign X currently has any of them for any scroll
